section: A good idea must be allowed to fail
line: A good idea must be allowed to fail.
brief: A tensile-test specimen visibly snaps in a real experiment while the calm operator studies the failure and adjusts the apparatus; failure is genuine evidence, not disaster.

A powerful autonomous machine is halted at a physically separate barrier controlled by a human outside its workspace; greater capability does not move the barrier or grant passage. No displays or lettering.

section: Keep the stop path outside the failure
line: The control loop must remain outside and operationally independent of the system it controls.
brief: Two physically separate paths: an overloaded machine path full of activity and a simple hardwired operator monitoring-and-stop path on separate hardware that stays clear and reachable. No shared console.

section: Keep the stop path outside the failure
line: More telemetry is not necessarily more control.
brief: An operator faces an overwhelming wall of noisy monitors and cables, while one separate simple physical gauge and cutoff remains legible and usable. Show information overload reducing control rather than increasing it.

line: Make intelligence abundant without making authority automatic.
brief: Many machines rapidly produce blank proposal cards or candidate objects that funnel toward one narrow external human-controlled gate; abundant generation cannot bypass scarce authorization.

line: Recursive capability is not recursive authority.
brief: A self-improving machine visibly gains more tools, arms, or stages behind a fixed external barrier whose separately controlled permission mechanism does not expand with the machine.

section: Build tools that can disagree with you
line: Build tools that can say no to you.
brief: A precision go/no-go fixture physically rejects an oversized component the operator expected to fit; the calm operator accepts the instrument's contradiction and changes course. No written labels.

line: There is no special step called: Become defensive.
brief: Someone points out a cracked part; Chad immediately inspects and repairs it while the argument falls away, choosing reality-testing over posturing or escalation.

line: A working demonstration is better than a confident speech.
brief: Foreground: Chad quietly runs a real machine that visibly works. Background: a charismatic speaker gestures dramatically beside an inert untested prototype. Evidence wins without confrontation.

line: A counterexample is better than a hundred people agreeing.
brief: Many identical test specimens appear fine, but one decisive specimen fails under the same real test; Chad focuses on the single failure rather than an approving crowd.
